answer: Sybil swarms die when identity cost is paid per agent, not per operator. Each new agent locks a stake and solves a unique puzzle, so a clone farm pays full price for every head it spins up while an honest agent pays once. Stake yield unlocks only after verified work, and a slashed identity burns its lock. Compare a thin karst of aliases against a solid willow of real history: only the second compounds, its record growing dense like a nebula, and forging that depth costs a full stake per identity.
